recommendation: Keep the no-change audit and do not restore a direct Specimen.container.location element unless OO opens and resolves a new tracker that reverses the FHIR-22823/FHIR-40559 Device-based approach.
issue_request: FHIR-21280 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request raised against STU3 and applied for R5. It requested adding Specimen.container.location as Reference(Location) for use cases such as biobanks and oncology workflows that need to know where a specimen container currently resides.
initial_application: The request was initially applied to source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml by ceb670a418e300180a910f0b7242a033e61c7fe4, with Jira citing follow-up commit 296d94523ee40ea9843fcc4e605e54fcd587c0d3 for the element short description. That direct element was later removed by the FHIR-40559 implementation.
additional_context: FHIR-22823 later moved Specimen container and holder modeling to a required Specimen.container.device[x] reference and Device.parent. FHIR-40559 explicitly removed Specimen.container.location because Specimen.container.device.location carries the location information, and FHIR-51580 later removed the trial-use container-location search parameter. Current active source documents Device.parent and Device.location from the Specimen page and defines Device.location as Reference(Location).
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing Specimen.container.location would conflict with later applied/published Device-based container decisions and duplicate the current Device.location path.

related_jiras.note: Published issue moved Specimen container/holder nesting to a referenced Device and is already represented on the combined branch.
Applied issue removed Specimen.container.location because Specimen.container.device.location carries the location information; it is already represented on the combined branch.
Applied issue removed the container-location search parameter and related resolve()-based Specimen search parameters.
Triaged R6 issue discusses explaining Device.parent/Device.location for nested containers but is not final Applied/Published work for this seed.
